journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
title: Enhanced Hydrogen Storage Capacity of High Surface Area Zeolite-like Carbon Materials
material_description: CA800 | nitrogen-doped zeolite-like carbon replicated from zeolite beta template ZTA by CVD of acetonitrile at 800 C for 3 h; zeolite removed with 10% HF
purification_method: zeolite template removed by washing several times with 10% HF; dried in an oven at 120 C (TGA residual mass typically lower than 3% at 800 C)
source_location: main p.5 (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2007, 129, p.1677), Fig. 4, curve a (CA800), star marker (adsorption branch)
notes: archive: fig4_a_seg1.json; digitized marker centre (pixel 214.1, 611.2). Branch from marker shape: up-triangle = adsorption, down-triangle = desorption (the caption symbol key is not rendered in the page images; assignment follows the usual key and the down-triangle line lying above the up-triangle line in Fig. 5A curve b). Star marker = coincident up- and down-triangle markers; the adsorption and desorption rows both take the centroid of the merged marker. Gravimetric IGA-003 (Hiden); degassed at 10^-10 bar (1e-05 Pa) at 200 C overnight (duration not numeric); buoyancy correction with carbon density 1.5 g/cm3 from He sorption at 323 K up to 20 bar (printed "1.5 cm3/g"). Basis not named by the paper; basis_inferred = excess by the gravimetric-with-buoyancy-correction default. This isotherm also includes a buoyancy correction for the adsorbed H2 (density 0.04 g/cm3), which moves the reported quantity away from Gibbs excess toward an absolute-type amount. Textural data: N2 sorption at -196 C (ASAP 2020) after oven-drying at 130 C and evacuation 12 h at 200 C; BET range: P/Po 0.02-0.25; total pore volume from N2 adsorbed at P/Po = ca. 0.99; micropore surface area and micropore volume (values in parentheses, Table 1) given without a stated method.
free_volume_calibration: He at 323 K (IGA, up to 20 bar); carbon density 1.5 g/cm3 used in the buoyancy corrections

material_description: CA850 | nitrogen-doped zeolite-like carbon replicated from zeolite beta template ZTA by CVD of acetonitrile at 850 C for 3 h; zeolite removed with 10% HF
purification_method: zeolite template removed by washing several times with 10% HF; dried in an oven at 120 C (TGA residual mass typically lower than 3% at 800 C)
source_location: main p.6 (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2007, 129, p.1678), Fig. 5B, H2 curve (CA850; same data plotted as Fig. 5A curve a), star marker (adsorption branch)
notes: archive: fig5B_H2_seg2.json; digitized marker centre (pixel 797.3, 285.4). Branch from marker shape: up-triangle = adsorption, down-triangle = desorption (the caption symbol key is not rendered in the page images; assignment follows the usual key and the down-triangle line lying above the up-triangle line in Fig. 5A curve b). Star marker = coincident up- and down-triangle markers; the adsorption and desorption rows both take the centroid of the merged marker. Gravimetric IGA-003 (Hiden); degassed at 10^-10 bar (1e-05 Pa) at 200 C overnight (duration not numeric); buoyancy correction with carbon density 1.5 g/cm3 from He sorption at 323 K up to 20 bar (printed "1.5 cm3/g"). Basis not named by the paper; basis_inferred = excess by the gravimetric-with-buoyancy-correction default. This isotherm also includes a buoyancy correction for the adsorbed H2 (density 0.04 g/cm3), which moves the reported quantity away from Gibbs excess toward an absolute-type amount. Low-pressure (0-2 bar) gravimetric isotherm of CA850; Fig. 5A curve a plots the same data (digitized values agree within 0.01 wt%, archives fig5A_a_seg*.json) and is not given separate rows. Its marker pattern and its 1.5-bar value match the Fig. 4 curve c run (I3), of which it is probably the low-pressure part; the paper does not say so, so it is kept as a separate isotherm. Textural data: N2 sorption at -196 C (ASAP 2020) after oven-drying at 130 C and evacuation 12 h at 200 C; BET range: P/Po 0.02-0.25; total pore volume from N2 adsorbed at P/Po = ca. 0.99; micropore surface area and micropore volume (values in parentheses, Table 1) given without a stated method. Pore size: PSD maximum ca. 0.6 nm (Horvath-Kawazoe, slit pores) stated for the carbons shown in the Fig. 2B inset (CA850, CB850h, CB850); range 0.5-0.9 nm.
free_volume_calibration: He at 323 K (IGA, up to 20 bar); carbon density 1.5 g/cm3 used in the buoyancy corrections

material_description: CA850 | nitrogen-doped zeolite-like carbon replicated from zeolite beta template ZTA by CVD of acetonitrile at 850 C for 3 h; zeolite removed with 10% HF
purification_method: zeolite template removed by washing several times with 10% HF; dried in an oven at 120 C (TGA residual mass typically lower than 3% at 800 C)
source_location: main p.5 (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2007, 129, p.1677), text section 3.2; abstract (main p.1); Conclusions (main p.7); plotted in main p.6 (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2007, 129, p.1678), Fig. 5A, curve b (CA850, volumetric)
notes: Text value "2.6 wt %" at 1 bar via the volumetric (ASAP 2020) method (also abstract: "At 1 bar, hydrogen uptake capacity as high as 2.6 wt % is achieved", and Conclusions). Same measurement as the plotted point near 1.0 bar of Fig. 5A curve b, but that marker overlaps an adjacent marker (unresolved pair centred at 1.014 bar, 2.564 wt%) and was not separately digitized; no digitized value is recorded. Branch assumed adsorption. Volumetric Micromeritics ASAP 2020, 0-1.1 bar at -196 C; samples evacuated at 200 C under vacuum overnight; free-volume determination not described. basis_inferred = excess (volumetric default). Textural data: N2 sorption at -196 C (ASAP 2020) after oven-drying at 130 C and evacuation 12 h at 200 C; BET range: P/Po 0.02-0.25; total pore volume from N2 adsorbed at P/Po = ca. 0.99; micropore surface area and micropore volume (values in parentheses, Table 1) given without a stated method. Pore size: PSD maximum ca. 0.6 nm (Horvath-Kawazoe, slit pores) stated for the carbons shown in the Fig. 2B inset (CA850, CB850h, CB850); range 0.5-0.9 nm.
